comparison: Perfect agreement on the main experimental finding (C1-C3, C37, C64, C73-C74). Both evaluations find strong support for trophic eggs affecting caste determination. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and experimental controls, while peer reviewers describe it as a 'striking discovery' and 'compelling study.'

Complete agreement on morphological characterization (C4-C5, C38-C45). Both find the morphological differences well-documented and supported. OpenEval provides specific statistical details (p=1.8×10⁻⁹), while peer reviewers note the methods are 'sufficient' without raising concerns.

Full agreement on biochemical differences (C6-C9, C55-C58). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval highlights strong statistical support (p<0.0001) and methodology details, while peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive characterization with 'sufficient' methods.

Strong agreement on RNA differences (C10-C11, C59-C60, C62), though OpenEval separately evaluates C63 (R5) and C61 (R6) while peer review groups all RNA/DNA analyses together (C10-C11, C59-C63). Both find the evidence sufficient, with OpenEval providing more granular statistical assessment.

OpenEval separately evaluates the negative result for piRNA (C63) as supported, while peer reviewers include this claim within their broader acceptance of RNA/DNA content differences without specific comment on the negative finding.

OpenEval flags DNA reduction claim (C61, C72) as uncertain due to marginal significance (p=0.045) and small sample size (n=5), while peer reviewers include DNA findings in their general acceptance of content differences without expressing concerns about statistical robustness.

Perfect agreement on lack of embryonic development in trophic eggs (C13, C46-C47). Both evaluations find this fundamental distinction well-supported by imaging evidence. OpenEval emphasizes DAPI staining methodology, while peer reviewers accept this as a defining characteristic.

Complete agreement that queens are primary trophic egg producers (C48-C51, C71). Both find the experimental evidence (n=12 queenless colonies) convincing. OpenEval emphasizes the species-specific nature, while peer reviewers accept this as part of species characterization.

Agreement on seasonal variation (C52, C93), though peer review also includes periodicity claims (C53-C54, C69) that OpenEval evaluates separately. Both find strong statistical support (p=9×10⁻⁶). OpenEval focuses on seasonal patterns specifically, while peer reviewers group all production patterns together.

OpenEval separately evaluates sequential egg-laying patterns (C53-C54) as supported with appropriate non-parametric testing, while peer reviewers include this within their broader acceptance of 'seasonality and periodicity' without specific statistical commentary.

Perfect agreement on survival analysis controls (C65-C68). Both evaluations support the conclusion that differential survival alone cannot explain caste effects. OpenEval provides detailed statistical reasoning, while peer reviewers accept the experimental design and analyses as 'sufficient.'

OpenEval separately evaluates the high proportion of trophic eggs (C69) as supported, while peer reviewers include this within their acceptance of production patterns and periodicity without specific comment on the proportion value.

Complete agreement on novelty claims (C12, C89). Both evaluations affirm this is the first experimental demonstration of trophic eggs' regulatory role. OpenEval notes prior correlational studies existed, while peer reviewers emphasize the paradigm shift from 'nutritional role' assumption.
